name: Our Lady of Mount Carmel
history: Mount Carmel in the Holy Land is where the prophet Elijah called down fire from heaven. In the twelfth century hermits settled there in honour of Our Lady and became the Carmelite order. This feast, their patronal feast, spread to the whole Church, and with it the Brown Scapular, a sign of consecration to Mary.
life: The first Carmelites were Latin hermits who gathered by the spring of Elijah on Mount Carmel and received a rule from Saint Albert, patriarch of Jerusalem, in the early thirteenth century. As the Crusader kingdoms fell they moved to Europe, including England, where they became friars. A cherished tradition holds that the English Carmelite Saint Simon Stock, praying for his struggling order, received a vision of Our Lady holding out the scapular, the part of the habit worn over the shoulders, as a sign of her protection. The vision is a matter of pious tradition, but the Church has long approved the small Brown Scapular as a sacramental, worn as a pledge of devotion to Mary and of a Christian life. The feast was kept in England in the fourteenth century and extended to the whole Church in 1726. The Carmelite friars returned to their old priory at Aylesford in Kent in 1949.
prayerTo: Holy Mary, Our Lady of Mount Carmel, flower of Carmel and splendour of heaven, clothe me in your protection as a mother clothes her child. Help me to live the faith I profess, to pray as the prophets prayed, and to die in the friendship of your Son. Amen.
penance: If you wear the Brown Scapular, renew your devotion; if not, ask a priest to enrol you. Spend ten minutes in silent prayer as the hermits of Carmel did.
meditation: Elijah heard God not in the wind or the earthquake or the fire, but in a still small voice. Make space today to hear it.
